paper.title_en: Quark orbital angular momentum from chiral symmetry breaking in QCD
paper.abstract_en: The flavor-nonsinglet (<math altimg="si13.svg"><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">−</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></math>) quark angular momentum (AM) in the proton is computed based on the effective spin-flavor dynamics emerging from chiral symmetry breaking by QCD instantons. The QCD AM operators are converted to effective spin-flavor operators expressing instanton-induced chiral interactions. A large negative orbital AM <math altimg="si5.svg"><msub><mi>L</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub></math> arises from the interactions of the quarks with the chiral mean field in the proton in the large-Nc limit. It cancels part of the large positive spin AM <math altimg="si4.svg"><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub></math> and reduces the total AM <math altimg="si14.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak">+</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, in agreement with lattice QCD calculations.
